Treatment summary
Treatment summary. The patient presented after a rear-end motor vehicle collision with comlpaints of low back strain. The
reported mechanism of injury is consistnet with the forces expected in a collision of this type, and a lumbar strain is a plausible
diagnosis. Over the course of care the patient attended 32 visits, many times the number usually seen for an uncomplicated strain,
with appointments occurring nearly every day. Additional body regions were reported several weeks after the collision and added
to the plan. Imaging and standard clinical examinations have been within normal limits. Nearly all documented findings rest on
the patient's own pain reports rather than objective measures. No prior injury to the lumbar area is known from available records.
Two similar billing entries recorded on the same date of service are currently under review to confirm they are accurate.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
